## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nerujātaka* (Ja 379), titled in English as *Mount Neru*, is a canonical tale in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to its traditional introductory narrative, the Buddha related the story at Jetavana concerning a monk who took meditation subjects from the Master and resided in a frontier village. Although the villagers initially revered him and constructed a forest hut for his residence, they repeatedly abandoned him in favor of various wandering teachers—first those advocating the permanence of matter, then annihilationists who denied immortality, and finally naked ascetics. The story opens with the verses commencing with “Ravens and crows”.

 The verses of the jātaka are also referenced in modern selections of canonical verse literature [Ānandajoti 2010].
